subject: Post-call procurement checklist & routing: Invoice vs. Card
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medistack.io>, Ava Collins <ava.collins@medistack.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: procurement checklist & next steps (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks again for your time today — helpful conversation. Quick recap and the asks we left with: 

- Primary decision to confirm: pilot payment method (corporate card) vs procurement (PO/invoice) for POC and path to enterprise after success.
- Procurement requirements mentioned: vendor onboarding form, W-9, SOC 2 report (or alternative attestation), preferred invoicing cadence (Net 30).
- Interest in marketplace procurement (AWS/GCP marketplace) to simplify vendor setup — Jordan flagged this as attractive.

Action items for Medistack:
- Confirm preferred payment route for the initial $12k pilot (card vs PO).
- Share PO contact and vendor onboarding owner if PO is required.
- If card is preferred, confirm any card limits / internal approvals that could block charge.

Action items for Redwood (me/Ben/Karthik):
- Attach vendor questionnaire and a short SOW for the pilot (see attached).
- Confirm whether AWS Marketplace can be used — we have a beta listing; will confirm implications for licensing and invoicing.
- Provide sample invoice and pilot pricing breakdown.

Attachments: Medistack_MA_Platform_SOW_v2.pdf (pilot SOW)

Proposed timeline: if card for pilot -> start in 1 week. If PO for pilot -> expect 2–4 week procurement lead time depending on onboarding.

If you can reply with the PO contact or confirmation on card, we’ll get the ball rolling.

Best,
Naomi Feldman
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com | (415) 555-0182

From: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medistack.io>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Ava Collins <ava.collins@medistack.io>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 16:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement checklist & next steps (PO vs card / marketplace)

Thanks, Naomi — good summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- For quick pilots <$25k we typically use a corporate card (Procurement ok with this), but any production rollout will need a PO and vendor onboarding.
- Our security team needs either a current SOC 2 report or a completed security questionnaire. We’ll pass your questionnaire to them — can you confirm the latest report availability?
- Marketplace preference: if Redwood is available via AWS Marketplace with consolidated billing, procurement prefers that route (avoids full vendor onboarding). Is your AWS listing limited to certain SKUs?

I attached a short internal note that outlines our procurement path for third-party vendors.

Jordan
Head of Platform Ops | Medistack
jordan.lee@medistack.io

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Sep 2027 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: pricing/flow options for Medistack (notes)

Naomi / Karthik — quick note after the call: 

- Pricing impact: card payments require upfront charge; invoices introduce 30–45 day receivable window and a slightly higher admin overhead. For pilot size ~12k the difference is immaterial; for multi-month pilots we should show both invoice and card pricing (invoice net prices but expect payment terms).
- Marketplace path (AWS) is the fastest for procurement to accept without vendor onboarding. If we can enable a marketplace SKU for the pilot that keeps the price consistent, that should be the default recommendation.
- Risk: marketplace fees / billing lag. If Medistack wants to avoid marketplace fees, PO onboarding is fine but ask for a committed start date to reduce gap.

Proposed next steps (internal):
1) Confirm whether our AWS marketplace SKU can be used for this pilot — I’ll loop with Marketplace team tomorrow.
2) Prepare: sample invoice, short SOW, W-9, security artifact note. (I attached the sample invoice template.)
3) Draft mutual action plan with timelines for card -> pilot in 1 week or PO -> onboarding 2–4 weeks.

Ben
Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwoodinference.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Lee <jordan.lee@medistack.io>, Ava Collins <ava.collins@medistack.io>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement checklist & next steps (PO vs card / marketplace)

Jordan / Ava — thanks for the quick turnaround. A few concrete items from our side to unblock procurement quickly: 

1) W-9 and vendor details — attached.
2) Pilot SOW and pricing — attached (Medistack_MA_Platform_SOW_v2.pdf). Pilot price shown as card and invoice options; see page 2.
3) Marketplace status — we do have a limited AWS Marketplace listing that supports metered and one-off SKUs. Ben is confirming SKU availability and any timing implications; our estimate is 3–7 business days to enable a specific pilot SKU if needed.

If you prefer to start immediately, recommendation: use corporate card for the pilot (fastest). Parallel path: we can initiate vendor onboarding if Procurement wants PO for the pilot — that typically takes 2–4 weeks but can be accelerated if ProcureOne is the vendor management provider.

DocuSign link for the short pilot statement (card pay or invoice pay) — https://www.docusign.com/placeholder/rdw-pilot-sign

Please reply with either: (A) card approval for the $12k pilot + card owner, or (B) PO contact + expected PO issue date and your onboarding contact.

Thanks,
Naomi
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: Procurement_Questionnaire_Responses.xlsx

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@medistack.io>

Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: procurement checklist & next steps (PO vs card / marketplace)

Appreciate the clear options. Quick answers from procurement: 

- For speed, we can approve the corporate card for the $12k pilot — card owner is Jordan (will route internally).
- For production or any multi-quarter contract we will require a PO and full vendor onboarding.
- ProcureOne is our vendor management provider; they can accept the vendor packet and W-9 directly. I cc'd them.

Next asks for Redwood:
1) Final pilot invoice sample (how the charge will appear) — needed for our AP tracking.
2) Link to latest SOC 2 or relevant security artifacts (if SOC 2 not public, a security questionnaire response is acceptable).
3) If marketplace is an option, confirm whether billing shows up on consolidated AWS bill and any delay we should plan for.

We’ll aim to charge the pilot on card this week once Jordan confirms internally. If you could upload the invoice sample and drop the DocuSign link in the thread that’d be great.

Thanks,
Ava Collins
Senior Procurement Manager | Medistack
ava.collins@medistack.io

Attachment: Medistack_Vendor_Onboarding_Form.pdf
